system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | At least **50% / AUD 12m** for general warranties, with separate higher or uncapped regimes for title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and pre-Completion obligations. | **Reject 20% and seek at least 50%** — the proposed cap is inadequate relative to the identified customer, IP, privacy and liability risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only excess is recoverable. | Lower de minimis (e.g. **AUD 10,000**) and a **tipping basket** of no more than **AUD 120,000–240,000**, with related claims aggregated and no thresholds for indemnities, tax, title or fraud. | **Counter with a lower threshold and tipping basket** — the Seller’s formulation can strand numerous connected losses and gives it the full benefit of the basket. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**; Seller seeks limitations applying to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties; longer periods for tax, IP, employment and regulatory matters; no short contractual limit for title, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Extend general claims to 24 months and expressly separate other categories** — 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge or a second audit cycle is completed. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same **20% cap and 18-month limit** as general warranties. | Title, capacity, authority, ownership and freedom from encumbrances capped at **100% of the price**, with at least a **six-year period** or no contractual time limit. | **Reject treatment as general warranties** — Buyer must have full recourse if Seller cannot validly transfer the 100% interest being purchased. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express carve-out is offered; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions are stated to apply to **all Claims of any nature**. | Express preservation of claims for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, deliberate concealment and wilful misconduct, including applicable statutory/ACL rights; no cap, threshold, exclusive-remedy or time bar. | **Insert an overriding fraud and deliberate-conduct carve-out** — a Seller must not obtain contractual protection for intentional deception or concealment. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records as at **5.00pm 22 September 2026**. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, in sufficient detail to identify the nature and reasonably assess the scope of the issue, against identified warranties; locked data-room index and refreshed disclosures at signing/Completion. | **Reject general data-room and public-record disclosure** — merely making documents searchable does not give Buyer meaningful notice of warranty exceptions. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by Buyer or advisers, including matters merely **discoverable** from the data room or public records. | Actual conscious knowledge only of a short list of named senior Buyer deal-team members, without enquiry, constructive knowledge or adviser imputation; Seller bears the proof burden. Specific indemnities should not be knowledge-qualified. | **Delete constructive/discoverable and adviser knowledge** — disclosure and diligence should not convert Seller warranties into Buyer-assumed risk. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, although DD-002 indicates consent conditions and no final consent or satisfaction evidence exists. | A true condition precedent requiring final written consent and satisfaction or waiver of all related conditions, in form acceptable to Buyer and without adverse commercial amendments, fees or termination rights. | **Do not permit deemed satisfaction by mere delivery** — Bluefen represents about **AUD 3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue**, making conditional or adverse consent unacceptable. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release is to be supplied **after Completion**. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, with binding payoff letter, release of all guarantees and security, control of lodgements, and debt deducted under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics. | **Make repayment and release a Completion requirement** — Buyer should not acquire a company still indebted or encumbered under Seller financing. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are said to be Seller’s matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | Bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs treated as Seller transaction expenses/debt-like items, paid by Seller or deducted dollar-for-dollar from price, with evidence of payment. | **Add the full grossed-up amount to funds flow as a Seller deduction** — Completion-triggered liabilities must not erode the agreed debt-free/cash-free value. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific **AUD 180,000 SOW3 payment**; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Payment and effective transfer of all SOW3 Project Materials as Completion deliverables, plus a specific indemnity covering ownership defects, infringement, inability to use, remediation and third-party claims—not just the unpaid fee. | **Expand the indemnity and require assignment evidence before Completion** — paying AUD 180,000 does not itself cure an ownership or chain-of-title defect. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not expected to be material; scope, access, notification duties and loss remain unresolved for approximately **1,240 records**. | Prompt forensic investigation, preservation and reporting obligations, Buyer approval of notifications/remediation, updated disclosure before Completion and a specific indemnity for all investigation, notification, regulatory, third-party and remediation costs. | **Require resolution plan plus a standalone indemnity** — uncertainty over access and notification is itself a risk and should not be neutralised by materiality or general warranty limits. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Full contracts and timing analysis; pre-Completion, accrued, unavoidable or Seller-committed amounts borne by Seller or reflected in price/working-capital mechanics, with no renewal or amendment outside ordinary course without Buyer consent. | **Do not accept the “ordinary course” label without allocation analysis** — the documents do not establish whether the costs are terminable, accrued or attributable to Buyer’s ownership period. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses apply globally to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, debt/leakage and fraud, with an express priority clause preventing general limitations from overriding specific protections. | **Reject the global “all Claims” construct** — it could inadvertently cap or time-bar the very protections negotiated for known risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification of issued capital and beneficial ownership, share certificates, constitution and historical allotments/transfers; ASIC and PPSR searches; releases of encumbrances; executed transfers and updated register at Completion. | **Treat the register as evidence, not conclusive verification** — it does not alone prove beneficial ownership, valid issuance or freedom from third-party security interests. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are said to be “settled” under the general **20%/18-month** regime. | A separate historical tax indemnity with an appropriate statutory-period survival and up to a 100% price cap; robust IP ownership, chain-of-title, non-infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignment protections, with longer survival and specific indemnities where needed. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open and outside the general regime** — latent tax assessments and IP ownership defects commonly emerge well after 18 months and can exceed a 20% cap. |

### Priority buyer positions

The principal **no-go items for Completion** should be:

1. Final satisfactory **Bluefen consent**;
2. Repayment and release of the **Riverlark facility and security**;
3. Confirmed acquisition of the **Ironquay SOW3 IP**;
4. Seller-funded treatment of the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs**;
5. Adequate investigation and specific protection for the **export/privacy incident**; and
6. Full **title, fraud, tax and specific-indemnity carve-outs** from the general limitations.
=== END ADVICE ===
